documents.title: REF: Reduce cognitive complexity of `tokenize_bytes`
documents.author: Alvaro-Kothe
documents.text:
REF: Reduce cognitive complexity of tokenize_bytes

The tokenize_bytes function currently has a cognitive complexity score of 551 according to clang-tidy, which significantly exceeds the default threshold of 25.

The complexity primarily comes from managing 16 distinct parser states within a single monolithic loop, combined with inline SIMD preprocessing and scalar fallback logic. Modularizing the state handling into smaller helper functions would help improve the readability and long-term maintainability of the CSV parser.

This is a good issue, but I think will invite unwanted drive-by.

documents.title: ENH: Refactor: centralize describe function selection
documents.author: vkverma9534
documents.text:
ENH: Refactor: centralize describe function selection

Feature Type

Adding new functionality to pandas

Changing existing functionality in pandas

Removing existing functionality in pandas

Problem Description

location : pandas/pandas/core/methods/describe.py

While reading through describe.py, I noticed that select_describe_func is called repeatedly (once per Series, and for every column in DataFrame.describe). Since this function is pure and depends only on the dtype, we could cache or centralize the dtype → describe-function resolution.

This wouldn't change behavior, but could:
reduce repeated dtype checks for wide DataFrames
make it easier to extend describe behavior for new dtypes in one place
The change should be low risk and internal-only.
If core team agree this makes sense, I'm happy to raise a small PR with a minimal refactor + tests.

Feature Description

Cache the dtype describe-function selection in describe.py to avoid repeated resolution when describing Series and wide DataFrames. This is an internal refactor with no behavior change, aimed at improving efficiency and keeping dtype handling centralized and easier to extend.

Alternative Solutions

_

Additional Context

_No response_

My assumption is that the work being done in the actual describe function (e.g. calculating all the statistics for numeric columns) will be take a lot more time than the functions to decide which function to use based on the dtype. So the performance improvements might not be very significant.

Not necessarily opposed to the changes you are proposing (it is entirely correct that this is doing duplicate work if there are columns with the same dtype), but you will have to show that 1) it gives a measurable performance improvement, and 2) it does not make the code much more complex.

Thank you for your consideration.

That's fair. I agree the actual describe_* work will dominate, so I don't exepct big wins here.

The main motivation is avoiding repeated dtype resolution for wide DataFrames with many columns of the same dtype, and keeping the dtype -> function mapping in one place for maintainability. But I agree it only makes sense if it stays very small and shows at least some measurable benefit.

I can put together a minimal benchmark (wide, homogeneous dtypes) and keep the refactor very lightweight. If the gains are negligible or the code gets more complex, I'm happy to drop it.

should I try raising a PR showing my improvements (in my purview) and see if something works out

Hi thanks for the clarification and for bringing this up in the policy discussion. Just to make sure I'm understanding correctly-> my takaeway is that #64002 is being referenced mainly as an example of a small reasonable refractor where requiring an issue first might add friction, rather than as a concern about the quality of this issu or my contributions more generally. If that's the intent, thanks for calling it out and please let me know if I'm misreading anything.

exactly correct.

I ran a quick benchmark on a wide, homogeneous DataFrame (10k float64 columns). on my machine, main took ~18.87s and ~18.63s with this change, so the diff is pretty small and within noise.

As expected, the runtime is mostly dominated by the actual describe computations, so this dosen't seem to give a meaningful benrfit overall. i agree it's probably not worth the refactor and I'm happy to drop this and close the issue. Thanks for the discussion.

REF: make _cast_pointwise_result an EA method

In the extension tests.extension.base.ops.BaseOpsUtil we have a _cast_pointwise_result method that is used to patch the result of Series.combine to do appropriate dtype inference so that we have e.g.

(There is also a test_combine_add method which does not currently use _cast_pointwise_result but could. Also test_combine_le looks like we implemented an entirely separate pattern for customizing dtype inference in that test. I'll look into seeing if these can re-use the _cast_pointwise_result pattern.)

This cast_pointwise_result should just be an EA method. ATM we override it in the arrow, masked, and string tests (I suspect that we _should_ be overriding it in the sparse tests but it looks like we skip a bunch of them instead).

This will effectively replace _from_scalars, which was a mis-feature. It will also let us de-kludge places where we use maybe_cast_pointwise_result and generally be more robust.

It also looks a lot like test_combine_add+test_combine_le are made redundant by more general tests in BaseComparisonOpsTests and BaseArithmeticOpsTests

documents.title: REF: simplify _constructor/_from_mgr/_constructor_from_mgr/...
documents.author: jbrockmendel
documents.text:
REF: simplify _constructor/_from_mgr/_constructor_from_mgr/...

ATM we have

_constructor
_constructor_sliced
_constructor_expanddim
_from_mgr (update 2026-04-14 this is )
<s>_sliced_from_mgr</s>
<s>_expanddim_from_mgr</s>
_constructor_from_mgr
_constructor_sliced_from_mgr
_constructor_expanddim_from_mgr

I suspect that we can make do with fewer of these, or at least simplify them (e.g. make some , , #51772, make downstream libraries never touch Managers, very slightly improve perf in the non-subclass cases). Some of these ideas are mutually exclusive:

ATM _from_mgr is a classmethod, all the other *_from_mgr methods are regular methods. The _constructor_*_from_mgr methods rely on self._constructor*, so could not be made classmethods unless those constructor*s also became classmethods. Does anyone out there rely on _constructor* _not_ being a classmethod?

_expanddim_from_mgr and _sliced_from_mgr are each only used once, in _constructor_expanddim_from_mgr and _constructor_sliced_from_mgr, respectively. Can we just inline these and remove the methods (maybe keep the less-verbose names)? If not, can we at least and them?

Can _from_mgr be made ? If not can _constructor_from_mgr be inlined into it?

The 3 listed expanddim methods are there just for Series.to_frame. We could get rid of all three and tell subclasses to just override to_frame. (Doing this would also make it easier to tell subclass authors to handle metadata propagation in to_frame xref #32860)

We can slightly improve perf for non-subclasses by changing if self._constructor is Series to if type(self) is Series at the cost of slightly hurting perf for subclasses.

Most extreme: we can make it so that a) (most) subclasses don't need to override _any_ *from_mgr methods, b) subclasses __init__ don't need to know how to handle Managers, c) we don't need the constructor*from_mgr methods and d) (most) subclass authors never touch Managers by writing e.g.

i.e. assume that the subclass __init__ knows what to do when given a pandas object.

writes that this would inconvenience geopandas since it does inference when given a DataFrame but not when given a Manager. In cases like that geopandas would need to override _from_mgr (why "most" is needed in a) and d) above), but ATM they need to override _constructor_from_mgr, so that wouldn't be a net increase in Stuff They Need To Do.

This idea is roughly #53871, which was reverted by #54922.

Just chiming in as a maintainer of a package that subclasses Pandas DataFrames and Series'. Apart from having many constructor functions and properties, at the moment it is also not very clear what a subclass can override, should override and must not override.

The documentation for subclassing ( ) only mentions ._constructor, ._constructor_sliced and ._constructor_expanddim. I would argue that there's no way around reading the source code anyway, when subclassing. But from the comments there, it's still very difficult to figure out how everything works.

Understanding the concepts here is fairly difficult if one does not actively participate in core development. And this has become more difficult over the last releases with the addition of new constructor related methods. Therefore, I am in favour of simplifying this system. But additionally, it would then be great to have some more documentation on the purpose of each function or property. Even if it's just in the form of comments in the code.

in #56175 writes [about removing constructor_expanddim_from_mgr and making subclasses override to_frame]:

for [...] clarity

The only clarity-related evidence I've seen is the comment above complaining about a) the quantity of these methods and b) their docs.

There will also be projects that are overriding this method (outside of geopandas)

I had claude search for these and it found

Several of these seem to subclass geopandas and IIUC (some of?) their overrides would be unnecessary if geopandas wrote type(self) instead of hard-coding GeoSeries.

Several of these need to keep _constructor_from_mgr for correctness. I'll throw in the towel on getting rid of that. AFAICT only geopandas (and its subclassers) need the other two _foo_from_mgr methods (for perf, not correctness). I think finding a way around that would allow us to get rid of 2 methods and simplify the docs situation for the large majority of subclass authors who don't need to care about these.

you and joris I'm sure are closer to the details here, but some observations.
There's an inherent requirement as it stands that subclasses need to overwrite _constructor_expanddim, _constructor_expanddim_from_mgr and _constructor_sliced - there's not a type(self) to use when going from 1d to 2d - unless you change the interface to requiring to_frame and squeeze to be overloaded by child classes or something of the sort. I agree that from the perspective of someone not super up to date on the pandas internals a shorter list of internal special things to override would be better, but I think documentation plugs this gap just as well from a pragmatic standpoint, even if it's not an elegant solution.

I only had a quick look and it does seem like some overloads downstream of geopandas are overkill with the current version (but they may support multiple geopandas versions, I didn't check)

Several of these seem to subclass geopandas and IIUC (some of?) their overrides would be unnecessary if geopandas wrote type(self) instead of hard-coding GeoSeries.

I think only trackintel and pynsee from that list do so? (spatialpandas has copied the approach from geopandas so it does similar things, but doesn't actually inherit from geopandas)
It can certainly be the case that we can make subclassing easier from geopandas, and I know we have had some issues (and improvements) related to that in the past (eg )

However, what suprises me a bit from looking at that list of sublclasses is that many of them actually override the _constructor_from_mgr method. It might be useful to investigate in more detail _why_ exactly they have to do so.
For example, autogluon is doing that to propagate their metadata (but should that be done automatically if we always call finalize after _constructor_from_mgr?) Similarly for timely-beliefs. tfs-pandas is defining _constructor_from_mgr to deal with the "not-fully-initialized" dataframe issue (after ).
swwm-pandas has the method to override the class (essentially calling self.__class__._from_mgr(mgr, axes)), but that does not feel as needed?

In the end, it has been our desire to move "construct from mgr" outside of the main constructor (which I still think was a good separation of concerns), but that inevitably complicated the constructors situation for subclasses. We can look into why / try to avoid the need of subclasses _having_ to also override _constructor_from_mgr in addition to _constructor, but in the end I agree it is also a matter of better documenting this.

Several of these need to keep _constructor_from_mgr for correctness. I'll throw in the towel on getting rid of that. AFAICT only geopandas (and its subclassers) need the other two _foo_from_mgr methods (for perf, not correctness). I think finding a way around that would allow us to get rid of 2 methods

I haven't looked in detail, but I _think_ that one reason is that many of those other packages are only subclassing DataFrame. It they would also be sublcasssing Series, I think they potentially need the equivalent _constructor_from_mgr on their subclassed Series for whatever reason they are having it defined on the DataFrame (eg to initialize an attribute, like pandas.Series._constructor_from_mgr does for the name).

Although that reason might have been true for pandas 2.1, but since we now hardcode to create a pandas DataFrame/Series from the manager (and not the subclass) in _constructor_from_mgr, and then pass that pandas object to the subclass _constructor, that might not actually be needed? (also not for DataFrame subclasses)

I think we've pushed this as far as itll go. Closing.

    df = DataFrame._existing_from_mgr_method(mgr, axes)
    if type(self) is DataFrame:

Removing _constructor_expanddim_from_mgr (even though used only once) feels a bit inconsistent with the other _constructor... methods, so I would prefer to keep that one just for consistency / clarity.
There will also be projects that are overriding this method (outside of geopandas), although I would generally guess they implement it with similar logic as _constructor_expanddim such that the change wouldn't impact results.

documents.title: REF/API: EA formatting methods
documents.author: jbrockmendel
documents.text:
REF/API: EA formatting methods

I went down a rabbit hole trying to unravel the many methods we have for rendering arrays. The status quo is not great (but not urgent). The methods I'm looking at are:

(EA|Index|Series|Dataframe).__repr__
Index.format (xref #55413)
(Series|DataFrame).to_string, to_html, to_latex, (maybe other Styler-like things im not familiar with?)
to_csv
to_json
(havent really looked at to_xml, to_stata, to_hdf, to_excel etc)

The pain points are roughly:

We special-case our internal EAs in ways that complicate the code and make it difficult to reason about. Some of these are just for perf, others actually break tests if we remove the special casing.
Keywords specific to dt64/td64 dtypes are used with our numpy dtypes but not for pyarrow dtypes or 3rd party dtypes. In particular I'm thinking of date_format in to_csv and in DatetimeIndexOpsMixin.format (xref #33319)
The boxed keyword in EA._formatter is documented as being True when rendering an EA inside a Index/Series/DataFrame, but the way it is enabled is via fallback_formatter in format_array may use it or not depending on spaghetti logic. Also for dt64/td64/period we _dont_ box the values in Series/DataFrame but do in Index/EA.
AFAICT this is largely motivated by the idea that eval(repr(index)) is valid, which i don't particularly care about.
Many of the code paths cast to object in ways that look unnecessary.
_Timedelta64Formatter and _Datetime64Formatter have a nat_rep keyword in __init__ that is never passed. The caller format_array does pass na_rep (which defaults to "NaN" and using it expect would break a zillion tests)
to_json just doesn't work with general EA dtypes (xref #35420, #31917, #32037)
date_format in to_json behaves differently from everywhere else (xref #16492, #22317, #39135, #47930)
General hodgepodge of mismatched keywords in different to_foo methods (most of which is unavoidable)

Some ideas on improving the situation:

A) Deprecate Index.format (xref #55413) and implement Index._format_flat and Index._format_multi for internal use. We don't use most of the existing keywords internally, so the new methods would be appreciably simpler than the current ones.
B) add relevant keywords (float_format, decimal, date_format) to EA._formatter to make the fallback_formatter spaghetti in 3) unnecessary
C) add a vectorized formatting method to EA with the same behavior as our internal EAs' _format_native_values. Then avoid special-casing our internal EAs in the relevant places.
      i) Note we used to have EA._formatting_values and i guess that was removed in favor of just _formatter. I think we could implement the default _vectorized_whatever in terms of _formatter so the new method would be optional for 3rd party authors.
      ii) The "relevant places" would include blocks.to_native_types (used in to_csv), to_json, Index._format_native_values, and format_array
D) Change the boxed behavior to box in when inside and Index but not in Series/DataFrame.
E) for 5, just accept/document that na_rep is ignored for these dtypes and you'll always get "NaT"
F) standardize the "date_format" behavior across to_json and other places where it shows up

REF: Replace args/kwargs in groupby.resample with TimeGrouper arguments

The args/kwargs to this method are currently documented as:

*args, **kwargs
Possible arguments are how, fill_method, limit, kind and on, and other arguments of TimeGrouper.

I think we should instead have these argument as being keyword arguments to groupby.resample and a test that ensures the arguments to TimeGrouper are a subset of the arguments to this method.

Also, it looks like some of these arguments, how, fill_method, and limit, are entirely ignored? But I haven't checked thoroughly.

cc

Do you happen to know when TimeGrouper was resurrected? It was deprecated in 0.21.0: (see and ).

But today, in main, TimeGrouper is a key member variable of class Resampler:

In the deprecation comments ( ), it appears that TimeGrouper was a relic of the old-school groupby framework and its functionality was integrated into the Grouper interface.

So, I'm super curious if it was never fully removed, if it was only "deprecated" in terms of being an exposed/external capability, or if it was gone and has returned. Does anyone have any insight?

at one point in pandas there were two separate TimeGrouper classes:

The deprecation was only for pd.TimeGrouper. You can still get a TimeGrouper today by creating a Grouper with the freq argument not None. This was never deprecated, and shouldn't be.

REF: Proposal: change DataFrame.to_excel to output unformatted excel file

Feature Type

Adding new functionality to pandas

Changing existing functionality in pandas

Removing existing functionality in pandas

Problem Description

TLDR;

Please indicate with a +1 if you are happy for the default DataFrame.to_excel to be changed to output an excel file without any bold or bordered style attached.

Description

The current action of DataFrame.to_excel is to produce an excel file with default bold and bordered styles for column and row headers:

A number of issues are attempting to address this:
#50336
#22758
#22773
#52369
#50991

In a recent PR (#53973) it is proposed to remove the ability to format excel file styles with DataFrame.to_excel and instead document how users can use the Styler.to_excel to create styles excel files.

This has a number of advantages:

Simplifies the code, since it is effectively a removal and additions of documentation.
Creates a more consistent Styler.to_excel (which uses DataFrame.to_excel) since an unstyled Styler wont produce this bold bordering by default.
Encourages users to use a more flexible tool for formatting.

appreciate input to gain some form of concensus to proceed.

Feature Description

Alternative Solutions
